title: This Frog Oozes Glue, Traps Ants in It, Then Eats Its Own Skin

scenes.text: This frog turns its own skin into flypaper.
The crucifix frog of inland Australia. Grab it, and its skin oozes a milky glue.
The glue beats non-toxic medical adhesives and sticks even when wet. Researchers have studied it for surgery.
Ants that bite the frog get stuck in it. Then the frog sheds that skin and eats it, ants and all.
Between rains it digs two to three metres down and seals itself in a cocoon, only its nostrils open.
Then it surfaces for six to eight weeks, catches dinner on its own back, and digs back down.

description:
The crucifix frog (Notaden bennettii) of inland New South Wales and Queensland exudes a sticky, elastic frog glue from its skin when provoked; biting insects get stuck, and the frog later sheds and eats the skin.
The protein glue works when wet and has tested stronger than available non-toxic medical adhesives. The frog spends dry spells two to three metres underground in a cocoon, surfacing for about six to eight weeks after heavy rain.
Would you want glue skin?
subject: crucifix frog
first_comment: It eats the ants that bit it, skin and all. Which animal has the strangest defence you know?
